# enlace_metering

Usage tracking **and** credit/quota access-gating for [enlace](https://github.com/i2mint/enlace) MCP connectors — the platform’s “usage & access-policy” layer, sibling to `enlace_auth` (identity) and `enlace_connector` (deploy).

Whether a principal may use a resource is a **strategy** (a pure function), and *recording* what they spent is a **separate** concern from *deciding* whether to let them. That separation is the core design principle (see Research below).

```python
import enlace_metering as em

# 1. record (the meter) — a durable ledger over any MutableMapping (dict here; a
#    dol file store in prod, growing to s3dol/sqldol untouched).
ledger = em.UsageLedger(store={})

# 2. gate (the strategy) — parameterized credit formulas, composable.
policy = em.per_principal(
    {"owner@example.com": em.unlimited()},          # owner: no cap
    default=em.require_all(                          # everyone else:
        em.per_call_cap(2.00),                       #   ≤ $2 per call, AND
        em.credit_cap(20.00, period="month"),        #   ≤ $20 / calendar month
    ),
)

# 3. enforce (the glue) — one FastMCP middleware over EVERY tool call, fail-closed.
#    (needs `pip install enlace_metering[mcp]`)
from enlace_metering import MeteringMiddleware
mw = MeteringMiddleware(ledger, policy=policy, allowed={"owner@example.com"})
# app = py2mcp.http.mk_http_app(refs, auth=AUTH, middleware=[mw], stateless_http=True)
```

## Why (the three concerns)

| Concern                                  | Where                  | Shape                                         |
|------------------------------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Enforce** — may this call proceed?     | `policy`               | pure `GatePolicy = (GateRequest) -> Decision` |
| **Record** — what did it cost?           | `ledger`               | `UsageLedger` over a `MutableMapping`         |
| **Glue** — identity + gate + write-ahead | `middleware` (`[mcp]`) | a FastMCP `Middleware`                        |

The gate runs **before** the ledger sees the event — enforcement is a distinct layer from billing. The core (`policy` + `ledger`) is **dependency-free** and unit-testable against a `dict`; only the middleware needs `fastmcp`.

## Policies (the strategy library)

All are constructors returning a `GatePolicy`; compose with `require_all` / `per_principal`.

- `unlimited()` — always allow (record only).
- `credit_cap(usd_per_period, period="month")` — prepaid/metered cap per calendar period (resets on the boundary).
- `rolling_window_cap(usd, window=timedelta(days=1))` — sliding-window cap (rate control).
- `per_call_cap(usd)` — reject a single call whose *estimated* cost exceeds `usd`.
- `call_count_cap(n, period="day")` — count-based quota (no cost model needed).
- `balance_gate(get_balance)` — true prepaid credits: deny when a host-managed balance can’t cover the call.
- `per_principal({email: policy}, default=…)` — tiered plans (owner unlimited, others capped).
- `require_all(*policies)` — AND / most-restrictive (first denial wins).

Forward-looking gating (deny a call that *would* cross a cap) needs a proposed-cost estimate — pass `estimate_cost=(tool, args) -> usd|None` to the middleware. Without one, caps block on already-accumulated usage (“you’ve hit your limit”).

## Ledger layout

Keyed `{principal}/{YYYY-MM}/{id}.json` so “what did X spend this month” is a cheap subtree scan. The middleware writes **write-ahead** (`started` → `done`/`error` under one id): a costed call never spends on a shared key without a recoverable trace. The store is injected, so it grows from a local `dol.Files` to `s3dol`/`sqldol` without touching callers.

## Caller secrets in error text

A failed call’s error is recorded in the ledger and re-raised to the client, and a provider can quote a key back in it (ElevenLabs does on a 401): the caller’s bring-your-own key, or the connector’s own key. So the middleware passes that text through a **redactor** first, and re-raises a scrubbed stand-in (same type where it can be rebuilt, else `ToolError`) with no chain back to the dirty original.

The default, `redact_secrets`, replaces in one pass, longest first:

- the value of every in-flight request header named like a credential (`Authorization`, `X-<Provider>-Key`, `-Token`, `-Secret`) with `<redacted:{header}>`;
- the value of every environment variable named like one (a `_`-separated `KEY`, `API_KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` or `PW` segment: `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `FAL_KEY`, `SHARED_PW_X`) with `<redacted:env:{NAME}>`.

So a new BYO-key header or a new provider key in the environment is covered without configuration. For a secret named otherwise, `MeteringMiddleware(ledger, redact=secret_redactor(env_names=["MY_URL_WITH_TOKEN"]))`; any `redact(text) -> text` works. If the redactor raises, the error text is withheld rather than recorded unredacted.

Each secret is also matched URL-encoded and per `:`-separated part (fal keys are `id:secret`), and any env var whose value is a URL with a password in it is redacted whatever its name. Names that describe a credential rather than hold one (`S3_KEY_PREFIX`, `SSH_KEY_PATH`, `TOKEN_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`) are left alone. A provider that quotes only a truncated prefix is out of reach.

fastmcp logs a failing tool’s traceback *before* the middleware sees the exception, so the middleware also redacts fastmcp’s log records (`install_log_redaction()`, a chained `LogRecordFactory`, so loggers created later are covered too): what reaches the connector’s journal is redacted the same way, with the in-flight call’s redactor. `redact_logs=("mypkg",)` adds the connector’s own logger namespaces; `redact_logs=False` opts out. `RedactingLogFilter` does the same for a logger or handler of your choice.

## Install

```bash
pip install enlace_metering           # core: policy + ledger (no deps)
pip install 'enlace_metering[mcp]'    # + the FastMCP middleware
```

## Research — how usage-based metering / quotas are built

The design follows the settled industry pattern: **entitlement/quota enforcement is a
separate layer from the billing meter** — enforcement decides *before* usage is
recorded [1][2]. Common formulas this package parameterizes:

- **Prepaid credits / credit blocks** — buy a bundle, burn down; blocks carry their own
  amount + expiry with priority burn-down [3][4]. → `credit_cap`, `balance_gate`.
- **Metered caps + real-time balance / grace** — per-feature quotas with live balance
  tracking [1][5]. → `credit_cap`, `call_count_cap`.
- **Token-bucket rate limiting** — tokens replenish at a rate; a request costs N; deny
  if insufficient [2]. → `rolling_window_cap` (the sliding-window cousin).

Keeping the decision a pure strategy (not baked into the middleware) is what lets a host
swap “owner unlimited” for “prepaid credits” or “monthly cap” without touching the
connector — the open-closed shape the enlace family favors.

### References

1. Lago. *How to architect billing systems to power usage-based pricing.* [getlago.com/blog/architect-billing-systems](https://getlago.com/blog/architect-billing-systems)
2. OpenMeter. *Metering and billing for AI, API and DevOps.* [github.com/openmeterio/openmeter](https://github.com/openmeterio/openmeter)
3. Kong. *Stop AI token overspend: prepaid credits in Konnect.* [konghq.com/blog/product-releases/metering-billing-prepaid-credits](https://konghq.com/blog/product-releases/metering-billing-prepaid-credits)
4. Solvimon. *AI billing software built for tokens, credits, and inference pricing.* [solvimon.com/blog/6-ai-billing-software-platforms-built-for-credits](https://www.solvimon.com/blog/6-ai-billing-software-platforms-built-for-credits)
5. Zuora. *Metered billing: architecture, metrics, and monetization models.* [zuora.com/glossary/metered-billing](https://www.zuora.com/glossary/metered-billing/)

# _autosummary/enlace_metering.html.md

# enlace_metering

enlace_metering — usage tracking + credit/quota access-gating for enlace connectors.

The enlace platform’s “usage & access-policy” layer — the sibling of `enlace_auth`
(identity) and `enlace_connector` (deploy). Three cleanly separated concerns (the
research + sources are in the README):

- [`policy`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#module-enlace_metering.policy) — the **gate** (strategy): pure `GatePolicy` formulas
  ([`unlimited()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.unlimited), [`credit_cap()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.credit_cap),
  [`rolling_window_cap()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.rolling_window_cap), …) that decide allow/deny *before*
  > a call runs. Enforcement is a distinct layer from recording.
- [`ledger`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#module-enlace_metering.ledger) — the **meter** (record): [`UsageLedger`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.UsageLedger)
  over any `MutableMapping` (a `dol` store in prod → grows to blob storage untouched).
- `middleware` — the FastMCP glue (needs the `[mcp]` extra) tying
  identity → gate → write-ahead ledger, fail-closed.

The core (policy + ledger) is **dependency-free**; the middleware is imported lazily,
so `import enlace_metering` never requires `fastmcp`.

### *class* enlace_metering.Decision(allow, reason='', remaining_usd=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A gate outcome. `allow` is the verdict; `reason` is a human-facing
explanation (surfaced to the caller on denial, and useful as a remaining-budget
note on approval). `remaining_usd` is set by cap policies when meaningful.

### *class* enlace_metering.GateRequest(principal, ledger, now, proposed_cost_usd=None, tool=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Everything a policy needs to decide one call.

`ledger` is the usage read-side ([`UsageQuery`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.html.md#enlace_metering.UsageQuery)); `now` is injected
(timezone-aware UTC) so policies are deterministic + testable; `proposed_cost_usd`
is this call’s *estimated* cost when the host can estimate it (else `None` — the
gate then blocks on already-accumulated usage, the “you’ve hit your limit” model);
`tool` is the operation name (for logging / per-tool policies).

### *class* enlace_metering.UsageLedger(store)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Append/overwrite usage ledger over an injected `MutableMapping`.

`record` writes one entry keyed `{principal}/{month}/{id}.json`; the metering
middleware calls it twice per call (write-ahead `started` then the `done` /
`error` update) under the **same** `id`, so the store ends with the final
entry (its `cost_usd` is what `spend_since` sums). Entries need at least
`principal`, `month` (`YYYY-MM`), `id`, and — for costed calls — `ts`
(ISO) and `cost_usd`.

#### count_since(principal, since)

Number of the principal’s entries at/after `since`.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

#### spend_since(principal, since)

Total `cost_usd` across the principal’s entries at/after `since`.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### *class* enlace_metering.UsageQuery(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

The read side a policy needs: a principal’s spend / call-count since a time.

[`UsageLedger`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.UsageLedger) implements this; a test can pass any
object with these two methods. `since` is timezone-aware UTC.

### enlace_metering.balance_gate(get_balance)

Deny when a principal’s prepaid balance can’t cover the call.

`get_balance(principal) -> remaining_usd` is host-supplied (a credit store).
Denies if the balance is non-positive, or (when estimable) below the call’s
`proposed_cost_usd`. This is the true prepaid-credits model — burn-down lives in
the host’s balance store; this only gates.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.call_count_cap(max_calls, , period='day')

Deny once the principal has made `max_calls` in the current calendar `period`.

A count-based quota (no cost model needed) — useful for free/rate-limited tools.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.credit_cap(usd_per_period, , period='month')

Deny once spend in the current calendar `period` reaches `usd_per_period`.

The prepaid-credit / metered-cap formula: a principal gets `usd_per_period` of
spend per calendar period (default monthly), resetting on the boundary. When the
host supplies `proposed_cost_usd` the check is forward-looking (deny a call that
*would* cross the cap); otherwise it denies the next call once already at/over the
cap (“you’ve hit your limit”).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.per_call_cap(usd)

Deny a single call whose *estimated* cost exceeds `usd`.

Needs `proposed_cost_usd` (the host must estimate); a call with no estimate is
allowed (nothing to compare). Pair with a period cap via [`require_all()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.html.md#enlace_metering.require_all) to
bound both the per-call blast radius and the cumulative spend.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.per_principal(policies, , default=None)

Route to a per-principal policy (tiered plans): `{email: policy, ...}`.

`default` handles principals not in the map (e.g. owner unlimited, everyone else
a cap: `per_principal({owner: unlimited()}, default=credit_cap(10))`). With no
`default`, an unlisted principal is **denied** (deny-by-default).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.require_all(\*policies)

Allow only if every policy allows; first denial wins (AND / most-restrictive).

E.g. `require_all(per_call_cap(2), credit_cap(20))` — bound both a single call
and the monthly total. With no policies, allows (vacuous truth).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.rolling_window_cap(usd, , window)

Deny once spend in the trailing `window` reaches `usd`.

A sliding window (e.g. `$5` per rolling 24h) rather than a calendar reset —
smoother rate control. Forward-looking when `proposed_cost_usd` is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.safe_key_component(value, , what='key')

A traversal-safe key component: reject empty, separators, `.`/`..`, NUL.

The ledger key is `{principal}/{month}/{id}.json`; every component is
caller-influenced (the `id` embeds the tool name), so every component is
checked. `what` names the component in the error message.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_metering.safe_principal(principal)

A traversal-safe, lowercased key component for a principal (email / `sub`).

Rejects empty, path-separator, `.`/`..`, and NUL so a hostile identity can’t
escape its ledger prefix. Identity is case-insensitive (enlace_auth mints
`sub = email`), so this lowercases too.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### enlace_metering.unlimited()

Always allow — the meter still records, but nothing is gated (e.g. the owner).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

# _autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md

# enlace_metering.ledger

Durable usage ledger — the *recording* half of metering.

Records one entry per metered call into an injected `MutableMapping` (a `dol`
file store in prod — which grows to `s3dol` / `sqldol` untouched; a plain
`dict` in tests), keyed `{principal}/{YYYY-MM}/{id}.json` so “what did X spend
this month” is a cheap subtree scan. Implements
[`enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery) (`spend_since` / `count_since`) so
policies gate on real accumulated usage.

**Storage-agnostic** — any `MutableMapping`; there is no `dol` dependency (the
store is dependency-injected). *Every* key component is traversal-checked, so neither
a hostile identity nor a hostile operation name can escape the ledger prefix.

| [`safe_principal`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.safe_principal)(principal)             | A traversal-safe, lowercased key component for a principal (email / `sub`).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`safe_key_component`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.safe_key_component)(value, \*[, what]) | A traversal-safe key component: reject empty, separators, `.`/`..`, NUL.      |

# _autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md

# enlace_metering.policy

Access-gating policies — the *enforcement* half of metering (deny before spend).

Usage-based systems separate **enforcement** (may this call proceed?) from
**billing/recording** (what did it cost?). The gate runs *before* the ledger ever
sees the event: entitlement/quota checks are a distinct layer from the meter that
records spend (see the package README for the research + sources). This module is
that gate — and it is a **strategy**: whether to let a principal use a resource is a
pure function `GatePolicy = (GateRequest) -> Decision` that a host plugs in, with a
library of parameterized constructors for the common credit-based formulas.

Everything here is **pure + dependency-free** (no fastmcp, no storage engine): a
policy reads usage through the small [`UsageQuery`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery) protocol (which
[`UsageLedger`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.UsageLedger) implements) and returns a
[`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision). That keeps the formulas unit-testable against a dict and reusable
outside any connector.

Progressive disclosure: default to [`unlimited()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.unlimited) or a single
[`credit_cap()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.credit_cap); compose with [`require_all()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.require_all) / [`per_principal()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.per_principal) for
tiered plans (e.g. the owner unlimited, everyone else a monthly cap).

### Module Attributes

| [`GatePolicy`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GatePolicy)   | decide whether `request` may proceed.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`credit_cap`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.credit_cap)(usd_per_period, \*[, period]) | Deny once spend in the current calendar `period` reaches `usd_per_period`.       |
| [`rolling_window_cap`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.rolling_window_cap)(usd, \*, window)      | Deny once spend in the trailing `window` reaches `usd`.                          |
| [`per_call_cap`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.per_call_cap)(usd)                        | Deny a single call whose *estimated* cost exceeds `usd`.                         |
| [`call_count_cap`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.call_count_cap)(max_calls, \*[, period])  | Deny once the principal has made `max_calls` in the current calendar `period`.   |

### *class* enlace_metering.policy.Decision(allow, reason='', remaining_usd=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A gate outcome. `allow` is the verdict; `reason` is a human-facing
explanation (surfaced to the caller on denial, and useful as a remaining-budget
note on approval). `remaining_usd` is set by cap policies when meaningful.

### enlace_metering.policy.GatePolicy

decide whether `request` may proceed. Pure — no I/O beyond
the injected [`UsageQuery`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery). Host apps register one per connector (or per
principal via [`per_principal()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.per_principal)).

* **Type:**
  A gating strategy

alias of `Callable`[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### *class* enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest(principal, ledger, now, proposed_cost_usd=None, tool=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Everything a policy needs to decide one call.

`ledger` is the usage read-side ([`UsageQuery`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery)); `now` is injected
(timezone-aware UTC) so policies are deterministic + testable; `proposed_cost_usd`
is this call’s *estimated* cost when the host can estimate it (else `None` — the
gate then blocks on already-accumulated usage, the “you’ve hit your limit” model);
`tool` is the operation name (for logging / per-tool policies).

### *class* enlace_metering.policy.UsageQuery(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

The read side a policy needs: a principal’s spend / call-count since a time.

[`UsageLedger`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.ledger.html.md#enlace_metering.ledger.UsageLedger) implements this; a test can pass any
object with these two methods. `since` is timezone-aware UTC.

### enlace_metering.policy.balance_gate(get_balance)

Deny when a principal’s prepaid balance can’t cover the call.

`get_balance(principal) -> remaining_usd` is host-supplied (a credit store).
Denies if the balance is non-positive, or (when estimable) below the call’s
`proposed_cost_usd`. This is the true prepaid-credits model — burn-down lives in
the host’s balance store; this only gates.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.call_count_cap(max_calls, , period='day')

Deny once the principal has made `max_calls` in the current calendar `period`.

A count-based quota (no cost model needed) — useful for free/rate-limited tools.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.credit_cap(usd_per_period, , period='month')

Deny once spend in the current calendar `period` reaches `usd_per_period`.

The prepaid-credit / metered-cap formula: a principal gets `usd_per_period` of
spend per calendar period (default monthly), resetting on the boundary. When the
host supplies `proposed_cost_usd` the check is forward-looking (deny a call that
*would* cross the cap); otherwise it denies the next call once already at/over the
cap (“you’ve hit your limit”).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.per_call_cap(usd)

Deny a single call whose *estimated* cost exceeds `usd`.

Needs `proposed_cost_usd` (the host must estimate); a call with no estimate is
allowed (nothing to compare). Pair with a period cap via [`require_all()`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.require_all) to
bound both the per-call blast radius and the cumulative spend.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.per_principal(policies, , default=None)

Route to a per-principal policy (tiered plans): `{email: policy, ...}`.

`default` handles principals not in the map (e.g. owner unlimited, everyone else
a cap: `per_principal({owner: unlimited()}, default=credit_cap(10))`). With no
`default`, an unlisted principal is **denied** (deny-by-default).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.require_all(\*policies)

Allow only if every policy allows; first denial wins (AND / most-restrictive).

E.g. `require_all(per_call_cap(2), credit_cap(20))` — bound both a single call
and the monthly total. With no policies, allows (vacuous truth).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.rolling_window_cap(usd, , window)

Deny once spend in the trailing `window` reaches `usd`.

A sliding window (e.g. `$5` per rolling 24h) rather than a calendar reset —
smoother rate control. Forward-looking when `proposed_cost_usd` is given.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]

### enlace_metering.policy.unlimited()

Always allow — the meter still records, but nothing is gated (e.g. the owner).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`GateRequest`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.GateRequest)], [`Decision`](_autosummary/enlace_metering.policy.html.md#enlace_metering.policy.Decision)]
